# Module M1 · Relating

<!-- GENERATED by tools/build.py from content/*.yaml. Edit the YAML, not this file. -->
**Source:** lecture1 (whole file) · **Lesson:** [lessons/M1-relating.md](../../lessons/M1-relating.md) · **Prerequisites:** M0

## 1. Learning objectives

- Classify relationships as one-to-one, one-to-many or many-to-many and read crow's-foot ER diagrams
- Explain primary keys, foreign keys and junction tables (and why ISBNs make poor keys)
- Query across tables with subqueries and IN
- Combine tables with JOIN, LEFT / RIGHT / FULL JOIN and NATURAL JOIN, predicting which rows survive
- Combine result sets with UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT
- Aggregate per group with GROUP BY, filter groups with HAVING, and sort the result

## 6. Common mistakes

- **C1.1**: the "honor system" (row n of one table ↔ row n of another); one big table with repeated authors
- **C1.2**: reading cardinality in only one direction
- **C1.3**: ISBNs as keys (size, leading zeros); changing ids
- **C1.4**: hard-coding ids; `=` when several rows come back
- **C1.5**: using `=` for a list (D1-04)
- **C1.6**: joining on the wrong columns (D1-01); duplicate rows from one-to-many joins (D1-02)
- **C1.7**: INNER JOIN where "every row" was required (D1-08); RIGHT/FULL need SQLite ≥ 3.39
- **C1.8**: silent meaning change if another shared column appears
- **C1.9**: different column counts (D1-09); operator order when chaining
- **C1.10**: WHERE on an aggregate (D1-07); aggregating without GROUP BY (D1-03); GROUP BY on uncleaned text
